intent: Let a user opt in or out of one independent option, tracked as part of a form's state.
typical_uses: An option independent of any other, where several may be on at once
A choice staged in a form that takes effect on submit

dont_use_when.situation: An immediate on/off with instant effect
Mutually exclusive options, only one of which may be on

invariants.text: `checked` and `defaultChecked` are both accepted; `defaultChecked` seeds the initial state and is ignored afterwards, and when `checked` is given it wins and the component follows it on every render.

`indeterminate` is independent of `checked` in the props, but not in what gets reported: while `indeterminate` is true the box renders the minus mark and `aria-checked` reads "mixed" regardless of `checked`'s own value, matching the WAI-ARIA mixed-state convention for a "some children selected" parent.

anti_patterns.dont: Put the label text where children would go
anti_patterns.do_instead: Checkbox takes no content; wrap the box and the label text together in `Label` so the two share one click target
A controlled box with no change handler never receives its own toggle back - pair `checked` with `onCheckedChange`, or drop both and use `defaultChecked` for an uncontrolled box

a11y.by: Base UI's own Checkbox primitive (role="checkbox", keyboard toggling, a hidden native input for form submission, aria-checked including "mixed") plus checkbox.test.tsx's own role/aria-checked/data-disabled assertions

onCheckedChange.states: onCheckedChange is a function called with the next checked value and event details, not a value
onCheckedChange.because: A function type has no JSON Schema representation. Its second argument carries Base UI's own change-event-details shape (a reason, the triggering native event, and controls to cancel the change or allow it to propagate), which only tsc can check.

inputRef.states: inputRef is a ref to the hidden native input Base UI renders for form submission
inputRef.because: `React.Ref<HTMLInputElement>` is a union of a ref object and a callback function - neither is expressible in JSON Schema. It exists so a consumer can read or focus the native input directly, the same input `name`/`value`/`uncheckedValue` submit through.

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
render.because: Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the checkbox's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - neither expressible in JSON Schema.

style.states: style accepts a function of the checkbox's state as well as a plain style object
style.because: Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state (checked, disabled, indeterminate, ...). A JSON Schema `object` would reject the function form, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through checkbox.module.css, not through this.

unexposed_parts.reason: checkbox.tsx renders it directly inside its own Root wrapper to draw the box and its two marks, the check and the minus that swap on the indicator's data-indeterminate state; it is not exported as a component of its own, so a consumer cannot reach or replace it independently - only the whole Checkbox.

good.title: Labelled checkbox, one click target
good.code:
<Label>
  <Checkbox name="terms" required /> I agree to the terms
</Label>

good.title: Indeterminate, for a "some children selected" parent

bad.title: Label text passed as children
bad.why: Checkbox takes no content - there is no slot for it. Wrap the box and the text together in `Label` instead, which is also what gives the pair one shared click target.

bad.title: Controlled with no change handler
bad.why: `checked` with no `onCheckedChange` never gets its own toggle back, so the box is stuck controlled and never responds to a click. Pair `checked` with `onCheckedChange`, or use `defaultChecked` instead.
